title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory for BusyBox ftpd directory traversal (CVE-2026-136442)
date_note: ZDI's advisory records the coordinated public release on 2026-11-24; the page gives no earlier public day.
summary: Zero Day Initiative's advisory ZDI-26-1069 describes a directory traversal flaw in the BusyBox ftpd service. ZDI says remote attackers can create or delete arbitrary files or disclose sensitive information without authentication. ZDI says it reported the flaw to the maintainer on 2025-07-31 and published it as a 0-day advisory on 2026-11-24; the page records no vendor response.
plain: ZDI has published details of a flaw in the BusyBox FTP server that, it says, lets unauthenticated remote attackers create or delete files or disclose information. The page records no vendor response.
exec: ZDI published the flaw as a 0-day advisory, and its page records no vendor response.
action: ZDI advises restricting interaction with the product, given the nature of the flaw.

validation.note: Single source: ZDI's own advisory. NVD and VulDB pages for the related CVE-2026-136411 (tftpd) could not be read (NVD page empty, VulDB 403).

review.note: title, CVE-2026-136442, 2025-07-31 report, 2026-11-24 release, no vendor response and mitigation against ZDI-26-1069
